area: Read, report, CLI: a solver's own unknowns
rule: spec.md:448 (clinic.staffing.care is 70 h); spec.md:540; napkin.engine.read ("each in its declared unit"); tests/reference/from_program.scale_at
what happens: A solver-local unknown reads with unit '' and in canonical hours: x, y, z declared in day read 0.1089, 10.89, 0.001089 (sum 11) while clinic.xs = x + y + z reads 0.458333 day. napkin run, napkin play and napkin sample print no unit for them (clinic.staffing.care: 70, empty unit column). Cause: engine/timeline/record.declared resolves clinic.plan.x to the solver part, which has no type.
what the rule gives: Each unknown in its declared unit: 0.0045375, 0.45375, 4.5375e-05 day (the reference interpreter gives these); care 70 h with its unit.

area: Read, report, session view, napkin run: named values the model does not itself read
rule: spec.md:223-227 (Y.outflow has .actual_rate summed over its flows; it equals sum(water.outflow.flows.actual_rate)); spec.md:131 and D10 (any named value can be reported); spec.md:163 (.mean, .std); spec.md:235
what happens: tank.water.outflow.actual_rate and .request and tank.spread.mean read Unavailable with the reason "'tank.water.outflow.actual_rate'" (a KeyError's text) unless some formula of the model reads them, then 3 L/h, 0 L/h, 2 h. At a stop the reason says the run stopped there. napkin run --value refuses them: 'no named value of the model' (exit 2). A flow's .capacity when it declares none gets the same bare path. Cause: plan.py makes an endpoint only for what the model names; Reader.value turns the KeyError (a LookupError) into Unavailable.
what the rule gives: 3 L/h, 0 L/h and 2 h on every path, whatever else the model reads; a missing capacity says that the flow has none.

rule: spec.md:634 (a retained formula(...) may name a later local: it is evaluated when it is read, after entry); D14; spec.md:727 and D7 (a formula that cannot be evaluated keeps its reason, the occurrence finishes normally)
what happens: The engine evaluates each formula local at the occurrence's entry. f = formula(x * 2) above x: L = 3 L fails the run at 0 h ('plant.job#0.x has no value yet'); g = formula(since(this.other)) fails it at 0 h ('the event has not started') though nothing reads it. The compiler accepts both (its own refusal of a plain initializer says 'a formula(...) is read later'), the reference interpreter runs both (seen = 6 L; g kept unavailable), and the spec's own case, a flow's request = formula(left / (2 h)), runs: fixed for a flow, cause left for a local (Occurrences._enter evaluates every name of made.initial).
what the rule gives: Both runs finish: plant.seen = 6 L from 1 h; plant.job#0.g is unavailable with its reason, and only a model read of it fails the run.

rule: spec.md:746-758 (a flow with several legs); napkin/commands/compile.py and docs/cli.md (print the diagnostics or a summary; exit 0 ok, 1 diagnostics)
what happens: napkin compile, with or without --json, ends in a Python traceback (AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'start'), exit 1, on any model with a flow with legs, the every-construct acceptance package included; napkin run on the same model works. Cause: commands/compile.summary reads flow.source and flow.sink of every flow.
what the rule gives: The summary of the program with the flow and its legs, exit 0.

area: A record of selected values: napkin sample, the run store (cold and warm), Request(keys)
rule: spec.md:99 and 328 (a keyed read); napkin/program/record.py "What a record holds" (it keeps what the requested values need, one rule for a run and a cut); D10
what happens: A formula with .by(field).at(x), such as the worked network's need = formula(this.base_need * Reading.instances.by(hour).at(t).factor), reads Unavailable ('the record keeps no history of r0.hour') in a record that names it alone, fresh and from a warm store; by(rank).at(1) likewise. napkin sample prints 'clinic.need: no spread: the record keeps no history of r0.hour'. where filters, links, literals and occurrences' .at(t) are kept. Cause: record.needed walks Plan.reads of a lookup, which leave out the members' key field.
what the rule gives: The same values as a record of every value: need 6, 3, 3 W at 0, 1, 2 h; first 6 W; a spread for clinic.need.

rule: spec.md:572 (check declared parameter types, units and entry bounds)
what happens: plant.take.start(20 L) with take = event(amount: L in [0 L, 10 L]): the oracle runs to the horizon (got = 20 L); the engine fails at 0 h. from_program gives the oracle's event only its parameters' names, and Run._register copies the arguments with no range.
what the rule gives: The run fails at 0 h: the argument is outside its declared range.

rule: PLAN change 15 (a stop shows the values asked for in their declared unit); spec.md:448
what happens: Session.view(['clinic.staffing.care']) and napkin play --value clinic.staffing.care raise AttributeError: 'Solver' object has no attribute 'kind' (traceback, exit 1). The cause of R01 on another path: session._declared resolves the key to the solver.
what the rule gives: The stop shows clinic.staffing.care = 70 h, not editable.

area: Diagnostics at a bound: a move, an argument, an edit at a stop
rule: spec.md:660 (the failure reports the amount and the unit); spec.md:572; spec.md:899; PLAN change 15 and Session.edit (an edit is in the declared unit)
what happens: Numbers are canonical, with no unit: a move of 5000 mL into [0 mL, 4000 mL] fails with 'would hold 5, outside its range [0, 4]'; an argument of 7000 mL against [0 mL, 6000 mL] with 'amount = 7 is outside its range [0, 6]'; an edit to 5000 (mL) is refused as 'right.water = 5 ... [0, 4]', one to 3 (days) as 'right.level = 72 ... [0, 48]'. The retirement message converts ('still holds 8000 mL'): kept on one path, not on the others.
what the rule gives: The numbers in the declared unit, with it: 'would hold 5000 mL, outside its range [0 mL, 4000 mL]', 'right.level = 3 day is outside its range [0 day, 2 day]'.

area: Triggers on a solved value that moves between moments
rule: spec.md:674 (first contact, also for a condition that reads a solved value; never polling in silence); G0, 'Fire triggers when their condition first becomes true' (find the first crossing, or diagnose it)
what happens: when this.staffing.care <= 60 h, care being 0.7 of a store that drains at 10 h/h, fires at 4 h (the horizon, the next moment) and says nothing; care reads 59.5 h at 1.5 h. The same condition over a formula of the store, or over the store, fires at 10/7 h. A moving flow rate gets the named diagnostic ('cannot be certified ... a result of a solver whose problem moves'); a solver's own unknown escapes it.
what the rule gives: It fires at 10/7 h = 1.428571 h, or the run stops with the named diagnostic.

area: Declared solvers whose input moves: bounds and infeasibility
rule: spec.md:19 and D0 (a feasible problem has its answer, or a diagnostic names the step); spec.md:252 (a store at its lower bound stops its withdrawals); spec.md:279; spec.md:542 (trial states are evaluations apart); spec.md:658 and program/record.py (a failure ends the record at its time); PLAN change 10
what happens: staff_hours: h = 100 h in [0 h,] drained at 10 h/h feeds the staffing solver. Horizon 10 h: the run fails, 'cannot answer at t = 10 h ... upper bound -2.66e-15' (roundoff); 12 h: 'at t = 10.0044 h ... upper bound -0.0443' (a trial state past the store's bound); 9.99 h finishes; without the solver the store empties at 10 h. In each failure the entry is at 0 h and every value after 0 h is unavailable; a solve truly infeasible from 7 h (outreach >= 30 h) is also put at 0 h, naming 7.00443 h.
what the rule gives: The draining model finishes (care 0 h from 10 h); a true infeasibility fails at 7 h with the record kept to 7 h.

area: Diagnostics: the text of an expression
rule: spec.md:664 (the max_active message quotes the gate as written: 'until this.cleared'); spec.md:658 (an execution error names the expression)
what happens: Quantities show as the program's call q(2, 'L'): 'waits at `until this.water >= q(2, 'L')`', '"plant.water / (plant.water - q(2, 'L'))": float division by zero' (Python's words), 'tank.drain.actual_rate <= q(2, 'L/h') cannot be certified', and in a frozen occurrence's reason. Cause: core/expr.text writes Python.
what the rule gives: The model's notation: 2 L, 2 L/h, and the division by zero in the language's words.

area: Declared solvers whose input moves: a bound reached at a moment
rule: spec.md:19 and D0; spec.md:662 (work due at the horizon settles under the same rules); spec.md:658
what happens: A store filled at 10 h/h to its upper bound 50 h at 5 h, read by a solver (care <= available, care in [0 h, cap]): napkin.engine.run raises SciPy's ValueError 'f(a) and f(b) must have different signs' (no record) when the horizon is 5 h, or when a stage is due at 5 h with a later horizon; 4.5 h and 6 h finish, and so does the model without the solver. Same area as R10 (declared.py, _segment).
what the rule gives: Every run finishes; care is 40 h from 4 h.
